units.title: 1 The Gilded Age and Progressive Era

topics.title: 1.1 What were the impacts of rapid economic growth in the US during the Gilded Age?

outcomes.text: Explain why city populations grew and the housing, transport, health, sanitation and crime problems that followed.
Describe immigration from Asia, Eastern and Southern Europe and Mexico, and the tensions between new and old immigrants.
Explain the impacts of nativism and Americanization, and anti-immigrant laws such as the Chinese Exclusion Act, Gentlemen's Agreement and Immigration Act of 1917.
Explain the growth of monopolies, trusts, corporations and robber barons, including vertical and horizontal integration.
Describe the major industrialists Carnegie, Morgan and Rockefeller, and how business lobbying affected politics.
Describe industrial working conditions and the aims and members of unions such as the Knights of Labor, AFL and IWW.
Explain union divisions over gender, race and immigration, and the impact of major strikes: 1877, Haymarket, Pullman and the 1902 Coal Strike.
Describe Native American resistance in the West, including the Dawes Act, Wounded Knee and boarding schools.
Explain the reactions of cowboys to development and why Exodusters moved West.
Describe the Grange Movement, farmers' alliances and the rise and goals of the Populist Party.

topics.title: 1.2 What were the main aims and policies of the Progressive Movement?

outcomes.text: Explain Progressive efforts to limit party machines and bosses, foster efficient government and the muckrakers' role.
Describe antitrust laws: Sherman Act, Federal Trade Commission Act and Clayton Act.
Describe product regulation through the Pure Food and Drug Act and Meat Inspection Act.
Describe child labor regulation: the Keating-Owen Act and Hammer v. Dagenhart.
Describe temperance and prohibition, key leaders Frances Willard and Carrie Nation, the WCTU and the Anti-Saloon League.
Describe the growth of suffrage associations and the roles of Mott, Anthony, Stanton and Stone.
Compare Carrie Chapman Catt's Winning Plan with Alice Paul and the Congressional Union.
Explain why politicians' attitudes to suffrage changed, including women's role in the First World War.

topics.title: 1.3 How successful was the Progressive Movement up to 1920?

outcomes.text: Assess the achievements and limits of Roosevelt's Square Deal, Taft's economic policies and Wilson's New Freedom.
Explain the reasons for and impacts of the 16th, 17th, 18th and 19th Amendments.
Assess the limits of Progressivism: unsolved urban problems, Social Darwinism and continuing political inequality.

subtopics.title: Race relations in the Progressive Era

outcomes.text: Explain the impacts of segregation, including Plessy v. Ferguson.
Describe race riots and lynching of African, Hispanic, Asian and Native Americans.
Describe civil rights activism: Washington, Wells, Du Bois, Garvey, the Niagara Movement, NAACP and UNIA.
Describe Native American resistance and reform calls, such as the Society of American Indians.

units.title: 2 American Imperialism, the First World War, and the 1920s

topics.title: 2.1 What were the causes and consequences of US territorial expansion in the late-nineteenth and early-twentieth centuries?

outcomes.text: Explain economic, cultural and nationalist motives for expansion: Manifest Destiny, the closing frontier, new markets and military interests.
Explain the causes and impacts of the Spanish-American War of 1898 and the idea of the white man's burden.
Describe Theodore Roosevelt's role: the Roosevelt Corollary, the Panama Canal, the Navy and the Great White Fleet.
Describe US foreign policy 1909-21: Taft's dollar diplomacy, Wilson's moral diplomacy and Latin American interventions.
Describe the anti-imperialist movement and the arguments of the pro-imperialists.
Explain debates over citizenship and status of territories, including the Insular Cases and the Jones Act.

topics.title: 2.2 Why did the US enter the First World War and how did the war impact Americans?

outcomes.text: Explain Wilson's wish to stay out of the war and the impact of unrestricted submarine warfare and the Lusitania.
Explain the growth of anti-German feeling, the Zimmermann Telegram and US entry into the war.
Describe mobilization for war: propaganda, rationing and conscription.
Explain limits on civil liberties: the Espionage Act, Sedition Act and Schenck v. United States.
Describe women's role at home and in the war, and segregation of the military.
Describe differing soldiers' experiences, the Great Migration, strikes and the National War Labor Board.

topics.title: 2.3 What were the causes and impacts of economic and cultural changes in the 1920s?

outcomes.text: Explain the causes of the 1920s boom: the war's legacy, Return to Normalcy, laissez faire, low taxes, high tariffs and easy credit.
Describe rising living standards and consumerism: advertising, installment plans and automobiles.
Explain economic difficulties: barriers to prosperity, farmers' troubles and declining heavy industry.
Describe life under prohibition, speakeasies, the rise and power of organized crime and the federal response.
Explain the clash of fundamentalism and evolution, including the Scopes Trial.
Describe changing gender roles, the New Woman, feminism and the flapper lifestyle, and opposition to them.
Explain growing intolerance: the Second Ku Klux Klan, immigration restriction and the First Red Scare.
Describe the Red Summer of 1919, racial violence and the Harlem Renaissance.
Describe Native Americans' status in the 1920s, including citizenship through the Snyder Act.

units.title: 3 The Great Depression, the Second World War, and the Early Cold War

topics.title: 3.1 What were the causes and impacts of the Great Depression and New Deal?

outcomes.text: Explain the causes of the Depression: overproduction, high tariffs, easy credit and speculation.
Describe bank failures, the Great Crash and rising unemployment among different groups.
Describe homelessness, migration and family separation, including repatriation of people of Hispanic heritage.
Explain Hoover's rugged individualism, relief attempts and response to the Bonus Army.
Explain Roosevelt's Three Rs of relief, recovery and reform, and the First Hundred Days.
Describe the First New Deal policies, such as the Emergency Banking Act, AAA, NIRA, TVA and Glass-Steagall.
Describe the Second New Deal: the WPA, National Labor Relations Act and Social Security Act.
Explain opposition from left and right, Supreme Court rulings and Roosevelt's court-packing plan.
Assess the legacy of the New Deal, including the New Deal Coalition and expanded federal power.

topics.title: 3.2 Why and how did US foreign policy evolve between 1935 and 1959?

subtopics.title: From neutrality to the Cold War

outcomes.text: Explain early US reactions to the Second World War: the Neutrality Acts, Lend-Lease and Pearl Harbor.
Describe Allied tensions at Yalta and Potsdam and the Iron Curtain in Europe.
Explain the impact of the atomic bomb and nuclear proliferation.
Describe the Truman Doctrine, the Marshall Plan and the Berlin Blockade and Airlift.
Describe the formation of NATO and the Warsaw Pact.
Explain the domino theory and the US reaction to communist China.
Explain the causes, US involvement, impacts and outcomes of the Korean War.
Describe Eisenhower's New Look, Khrushchev's Peaceful Coexistence, the Suez Crisis and the Eisenhower Doctrine.
Describe the space race to launch a satellite.

topics.title: 3.3 Why and how far did US society change in the 1940s and 1950s?

outcomes.text: Explain the impact of the GI Bill, consumerism, the Baby Boom and the suburbs, and the role of government economic policy.
Describe women's role in the war and the return to conservative family and gender norms.
Describe the rise of religion, mass evangelism and televised church services.
Describe youth culture resisting norms: automobiles, Beatniks, media and rock and roll.
Explain Joseph McCarthy's beliefs and role and the House Un-American Activities Committee.
Describe anti-communist legislation and the Red Scare's impact on political discourse.
Describe race relations in the Second World War: riots, the Double-V Campaign and Japanese American internment.
Describe civil rights groups and leaders: NAACP, CORE, SCLC, Farmer, Randolph, Rustin, Marshall and King.
Describe Southern responses: the Montgomery Bus Boycott, Southern Manifesto, sit-ins and Little Rock Nine.
Explain the impact of federal actions and Supreme Court cases such as Brown v. Board and the Civil Rights Act of 1957.

units.title: 4 The Development of the US in the 1960s and 1970s

topics.title: 4.1 Why and how did US approaches to the Cold War change between 1961 and 1979?

outcomes.text: Explain Kennedy's flexible response.
Explain the Bay of Pigs Invasion and its impact.
Explain the Berlin Crisis and its impact.
Explain the Cuban Missile Crisis and its impact.
Explain the origins of the Vietnam War and why the US entered.
Describe Johnson's escalation, the Gulf of Tonkin Resolution and Operation Rolling Thunder.
Explain the Tet Offensive's impact on strategy and public opinion.
Describe Nixon's Vietnamization, the Paris Peace Accords and the war's outcome.
Explain why Nixon sought detente.
Describe detente policies towards China and the USSR.
Describe SALT, SALT II and the Helsinki Agreement.
Explain the US reaction to the Soviet invasion of Afghanistan.

topics.title: 4.2 Why and how did politics in the US evolve between 1960 and 1979?

outcomes.text: Compare domestic policies: Kennedy's New Frontier, Johnson's Great Society, Nixon's New Economic Policy and Southern Strategy.
Explain the economic challenges under Ford and Carter.
Describe the New Left, student organizations and divisions in the Democratic Party.
Describe the Republican Party and the Silent Majority, and the counterculture's impact.
Explain the importance of television to the anti-war movement.
Explain the credibility gap, the Pentagon Papers and Watergate.
Explain the imperial presidency and the anti-war movement's impact on political discourse.

topics.title: 4.3 Why and how far did the position of minorities improve in the US between 1960 and 1979?

outcomes.text: Describe key leaders: King, Carmichael, Malcolm X, Chavez, Huerta and Banks.
Describe activist groups: Black Power, Black Panthers, Rainbow Coalition, Chicano movement, AIM and Asian American Political Alliance.
Explain the impact of key legislation: Civil Rights Acts, Voting Rights Act and Immigration and Nationality Act.
Explain the impact of Supreme Court cases: Gideon, Loving and Bakke.
Describe Betty Friedan, the National Organization for Women and the women's liberation movement's fight for the ERA.
Describe gender equality gains through Congress and courts, including Title IX and Roe v. Wade.
Describe the gay rights movement: Stonewall, the Gay Liberation Front and the 1979 national march.
Explain resistance to change: the anti-feminist movement, late-1960s race riots, the Kerner Report and the religious right.

topics.title: 5.1 Why and how did the global role of the US evolve between 1980 and 2008?

subtopics.title: End of the Cold War and globalization

outcomes.text: Explain Reagan's abandonment of detente and the impact of Gorbachev and his relationship with Reagan.
Describe the Iran-Contra affair, the fall of the Berlin Wall and the collapse of the USSR.
Explain the impacts of globalization on foreign policy: the EU, China's growth, the G8, the WTO and NAFTA.

subtopics.title: Post-Cold War and the War on Terror

outcomes.text: Describe the Persian Gulf crisis and the US reaction to Iraq's invasion of Kuwait, including the trade embargo.
Describe NATO expansion and US intervention in the breakup of Yugoslavia.
Explain Clinton's motives for attacking Al Qaeda bases.
Explain the outcomes of 9/11, the Patriot Act and Homeland Security Act.
Describe attacks on Al Qaeda and the Taliban, the invasion of Iraq and the Bush Doctrine.

topics.title: 5.2 Why and how did US politics change between 1980 and 2008?

outcomes.text: Describe the New Right, Moral Majority, Reagan Coalition and Reaganomics.
Describe George H. W. Bush's domestic policies and the role of cultural issues in party politics.
Describe Clinton's third way, health care and welfare reform, the boom, NAFTA, deficit reduction and impeachment.

subtopics.title: Bush and the election of Obama

outcomes.text: Describe the disputed 2000 election, tax cuts and the growing deficit under George W. Bush.
Explain Bush's response to 9/11 and Hurricane Katrina.
Explain Obama's background and 2008 campaign promises.
Explain how the Great Recession and the Iraq war affected the 2008 election.

topics.title: 5.3 Why and how far did US society change between 1980 and 2008?

outcomes.text: Describe the digital revolution: personal computers, mobile phones, the internet, social media and robotics.
Explain the growth of multiculturalism and minority populations, including the 2000 census.
Explain the causes of rising immigration from Latin America, the Caribbean and Asia.
Describe the fight for and passage of the Americans with Disabilities Act.
Describe continuing inequalities for ethnic minorities and events such as the 1992 riots and the Million Man March.
Describe the growth of the LGBT rights movement and the impact of feminism in the 1980s and 90s.
Explain conservative reactions to the AIDS epidemic and debates over immigration and nativism.
Explain opposition to multiculturalism, affirmative action (Proposition 209) and the LGBT movement.
